subject: Elon Musk's recorded 2016 remarks about Tesla Autopilot
called_fake_by: Tesla's lawyers, in the wrongful-death suit over Walter Huang's 2018 crash (they raised it as a possibility)
claim: Huang's family wanted to question Musk under oath about his 2016 claims for Autopilot, including recorded conference remarks. Tesla's lawyers said Musk couldn't recall the details. They also raised the possibility that recordings of him could be deepfakes, since he is a frequent target. They didn't point to any specific recording as altered.
finding: The cited reporting describes no evidence that any recording was altered. Judge Evette Pennypacker called the argument deeply troubling, saying it would let famous people avoid owning what they said. Her order didn't rule on authenticity. (A separate 2016 Tesla promo video was a different matter: a Tesla engineer testified that it was staged.)
outcome: The judge tentatively ordered a deposition of Musk. Tesla settled with the Huang family in April 2024, on the eve of trial. The terms weren't disclosed.

sources.title: People are trying to claim real videos are deepfakes. The courts are not amused
Elon Musk will likely testify about his Autopilot statements
